title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, resume, and server timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints were not consistently handling client-side cancels and transport disconnects which led to leaked KV-cache state, stuck in-flight tokens, and inconsistent function/tool-calling behavior for resumed streams. This PR implements a set of lifecycle controls: 1) explicit client cancel handling where the server consumes an abort signal (http2/httptwo CANCEL/connection close/SSE disconnect) and transitions the generation to CANCELLED state, freeing any KV cache and emitting a cancellation trace span; 2) graceful disconnect handling that marks the session as disconnected but allows short reconnect windows for resume; 3) a resumable streaming token protocol (Stream-Resume header + resume token) allowing clients to reconnect and request continuation from last-acknowledged token index when backend generation is still available; 4) server-side hard timeouts and soft timeouts with configurable grace periods to avoid unbounded resource retention; 5) plumbing cancel semantics into the OpenAI-compat layer so third-party clients using openai-compatible endpoints observe identical lifecycle semantics. Changes are backwards-compatible by default. See rollout notes for opt-in flags and compatibility knobs.

add resume token generator and verifier

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can you clarify how resume tokens avoid replay attacks? Suggest including a short TTL+nonce and HMAC.
Aisha Patel: Implemented signed resume tokens (HMAC with service key) with 10min default TTL, documented in streaming_lifecycle.md.
Samantha Lee: What happens if backend rolled over and KV cache no longer available at resume? We should return a deterministic error and suggest client re-request full context.
Aisha Patel: Added explicit 410 Resume-Expired response with guidance; client library will fall back to new request path in SDKs.
Oliver Grant: Performance concern: freeing KV cache immediately on disconnect could increase recompute for short reconnects. Can we add a configurable grace window?
Aisha Patel: Added soft timeout (grace window) configurable per-route via defaults.yaml; hard timeout still enforces max retention.
Samantha Lee: Please add metrics for cancelled_by_client and resume_success/fail counts.
Aisha Patel: Added streaming_metrics.go and increment points where lifecycle transitions happen.
Miguel Torres: Approve after addressing docs and adding a quickstart example for openai-compat resume.
Aisha Patel: Updated docs and added e2e fixture. Marking as ready for squash-merge.
release_notes: Added streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel handling, disconnect/resume flow with signed resume tokens, soft and hard server timeouts, and OpenAI-compat layer mapping for cancel/resume semantics. Backwards-compatible defaults; see streaming_lifecycle.md for migration and config.
testing: Unit tests for supervisor and kv_cache, integration tests for disconnect/resume scenarios, e2e fixture that simulates flaky network and verifies resume semantics. CI integration streaming suite was flaky initially due to timing; added retries and deterministic clocks in tests.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime.streaming.lifecycle flag. Start dark launches in dedicated clusters for 48h, then enable for 10% of hosted traffic with additional metrics alerting on resume_failures and increased latency, then full rollout pending metrics and SRE signoff.
notes: This also resolves ENG-1123 (streaming disconnect resource leak) and ENG-1189 (inconsistent function call completion on reconnect). OpenAI-compat clients will observe improved behavior when using resume headers; SDKs updated in follow-up PRs for automatic resume token handling.
